exercise.name: Sled Push
steps: Grip the sled handles and lean in at a low angle, arms bent.
Drive with short, powerful steps, pushing through the balls of your feet.
Keep your back flat and push until you cover the distance.
exercise.one_line_summary: Hands on the two upright poles of a loaded push sled, arms bent, body leaning in at about 45 deg with a flat back; legs mid-stride, the drive leg straight behind on the ball of the foot, the other knee forward under the body. The two pictures are the two strides. Quads are the target; glutes and calves help.

setup.target: Body leaning in about 45 deg from vertical, back flat, head up.
setup.why: Library step 1 (lean in at a low angle) and step 3 (back flat).

setup.target: Both fists on the poles, arms bent, about chest height.

movement.measure: knee bend of the back leg
knee bend of the forward leg
movement.start: ~90 deg, knee ahead of the foot
movement.path: Short steps on the balls of the feet.

muscles.emg: Vastus lateralis rises with sled load (S1).
muscles.role: Straightens the knee to drive the body forward.
muscles.surface: Front of the thigh, hip to knee.

muscles.emg: Hip drive (library secondary; S2: sled pushes train the sprint drive).
muscles.role: Extends the hip of the drive leg.
Pushes through the ball of the foot.

mistakes.why_it_matters: Library step 1 says lean in at a low angle.

sources.citation: Martinez-Serrano A, Marin-Cascales E, Spyrou K, Freitas TT, Alcaraz PE. 2021. Electromyography, stiffness and kinematics of resisted sprint training in the specialized SKILLRUN treadmill using different load conditions in rugby players. Sensors 21(22):7482. doi:10.3390/s21227482
sources.what_it_gave: Sled push at 20-90% body mass: heavier loads raised vastus lateralis and gastrocnemius activity (not biceps femoris) and changed joint angles.

sources.citation: Pino-Mulero V, Soriano MA, Giuliano F, Gonzalez-Garcia J. 2025. Effects of a priming session with heavy sled pushes on neuromuscular performance and perceived recovery in soccer players. Biol Sport 42(1):59-66. doi:10.5114/biolsport.2025.139082
sources.what_it_gave: Heavy sled pushes improved 20 m sprint and jump 24 h later: the push trains the leg drive.
The steps the app shows; the pictures must match them.

clip_check.check: Drive foot on its ball, other foot on the floor
Quads strongest red; glutes, calves lighter
